title: [3.x] `Bullet` and `GodotPhysics` - fix waking up neighbors when moving bodies manually (3D)
body:
Supersedes #124149

This PR fixes a number of bugs in different situations where operations with static and kinematic bodies does not wake other bodies that are touching or in the vicinity.

## Situations that were bugged previously:

### 1) movement forward via `set_transform` into sleeping bodies
Continually moving a body via `set_transform()` (or similar) will now wake other bodies as it hits them.
This now has a closer match to the behaviour of `GodotPhysics` (in 3.x) and `Jolt` (in 4.x).

### 2) deleting wakes rigid bodies
If you, for example, `queue_free()` a platform, boxes sitting on it will now fall.

### 3) transporting away wakes sleeping bodies
If you, for example, move a platform to a different location, any boxes sitting on it will fall.

### 4) disabling shapes wakes sleeping bodies
If you disable the shape of a body (e.g. a platform), any paired objects will be awoken - however see below.

## Bullet:
- [x] Movement forward - fixed
- [x] Deleting wakes rigid bodies - fixed
- [x] Transporting away wakes - fixed
- [x] Disabling shapes wakes - fixed   

## `GodotPhysics`:
- [x] Movement forward - worked already
- [x] Deleting wakes rigid bodies - fixed
- [x] Transporting away wakes - worked already
- [x] Disabling shapes wakes - fixed   


### Note
Disabling shapes in Bullet isn't 100% reliable in my tests: pushing a rigid body over a platform may (curiously) result in it not being paired with the platform in the bullet broadphase. Not sure why this is, whether the margins are too small, or it is related to the final velocity direction being away from the platform etc. The behaviour is still a lot better than previous though.

## Before / After PR

[WakeNeighbours2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33150388/WakeNeighbours2.zip)

### Before
Moving the `KinematicBody` into a sleeping `RigidBody` doesn't  wake it.
Removing the platform `StaticBody` doesn't wake the `RigidBody`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82a92f58-0eeb-4581-84aa-ef4e161c431f

### After
Moving the `KinematicBody` into the sleeping `RigidBody` wakes it.
Removing the platform wakes it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/764f9be9-906e-4153-9e0e-d91d9180b825

## This PR explanation
With any move, there are two AABBs to consider. The _previous_ AABB, and the _new_ AABB (after the new transform is set). Ideally we would ensure any paired objects in both AABBs are awoken, in any move. However, this does duplicate some work iterating the neighbours, as in most small continuous moves the same neighbours from the previous AABB will already have been awoken in the _last_ moves _new_ AABB.

For this reason we add an optimization to prevent this double work, we keep a record of the last tick each body was moved. If it is in continuous motion, there's no need to awaken neighbours in the previous AABB. If it is _not_ in continuous motion, we do handle the previous, in case any bodies there have been sent to sleep since the last move. (We check against the previous tick ID, but it's possible we could use an older tick, however, most of the benefit will occur even just using the previous tick.)

### `RigidBodies`
It turns out that with regular rigid bodies, the data flow is one-way, from Bullet to Godot, so `body_set_transform()` is not called (except in the case of teleportation), so there is no change to performance.

### `Kinematic` move_and_slide
Where these objects are in continuous motion, there will be no _previous_ AABB check applied (as with statics and kinematics), thus there should be no change to performance.
